_comment: #979, epic #969, ADR 0005: the rule language of the outer network wall, as examples both implementations must answer alike. The hosted Dispatcher's rule code is dispatcher/src/network/rule.ts (the schema `NetworkRuleSchema` and `policyFor`, which makes the second wall's list of names); the local Dispatcher's outer proxy is runner/src/code_reviewer_runner/factory_runner/firecracker/outer_rule.py (the contract's rule read by implementer/network_rule.py `parse_rule`, and `allow_list`, the same list for a VM on a customer's machine). Both suites read this file (dispatcher/src/network/network-examples.test.ts, runner/tests/unit/test_firecracker_outer_rule.py) and must give the answers below. `rules`: whether a rule document is a rule. `allowLists`: the names a narrowed VM may reach for a rule (a set: GitHub, the model provider's host, the app's host and the rule's own hosts; the hosted list also holds the Dispatcher's own host, which a local machine has none of; `null`: the rule `open` is not narrowed, the wide rule stays). `verdicts`: whether the narrowed wall lets a connection to `host`:`port` through by the list of `allowLists` entry `list`, with ONE matching rule written down here and applied by both tests: a name matches an entry that is exactly it, or a `*.suffix` entry when it is strictly below the suffix (`*.pythonhosted.org` matches `files.pythonhosted.org`, never `pythonhosted.org`); only the ports 80 and 443 go through; an IP address (any spelling) is never a name. Names are lower-case ASCII here (the proxy brings a name to that form before it compares).

rules.name: a list with an exact name and a suffix
a list that names a host twice
an address in the old numeric form
a name with a trailing dot
a wildcard that is not first
a label that starts with a hyphen
a last label that is a number
a host that is no text
a field the contract does not have

allowLists.name: off keeps GitHub, the model provider and the app
a list adds its own hosts, a suffix as it is
a name that is already there is not there twice
